evidence: bandAxis's docstring and bandItemFor's doc claim nests 'fold the same way', yet every test address was one step; db6f91d adds two-step addresses checked against the fold, ordering, and the >1 wrap. The agent rightly pinned the wrap as designed instead of forbidding it as the reviewer half-suggested.
guidance_note: When a docstring claims a function handles a shape (multi-level addresses), add a test of that shape in the same PR instead of only testing the degenerate one-step case.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: db6f91d only exported LEVEL_DECAY and added a decor test, while the stale 'a row then a closed group' rides:false fixture and its comment come from the original PR's switch to opens-based lowering. The edit-chrome comment was updated in that PR but the help-disclosure test describing the old when-gated sibling body was not; 539e39d flips it to true and adds a genuinely gated row.
guidance_note: When a PR changes a lowering and rewrites the explanatory comment at the source, grep the tests for fixtures and comments describing the old lowering and update them in the same commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 539e39d touched only test/help-disclosure.test.ts, and the hunk shows the original PR added the `text` parameter with the harness passing `undefined` everywhere. efe83f9 threads `text` through the harness and adds both the fallback case and the authored-fg-wins case.
guidance_note: When adding a parameter to a unit under test, extend the test harness to vary it and add a case with a defined value, rather than threading a constant undefined.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 539e39d did not touch CLAUDE.md. The 'those lines wear `band`' sentence came from the original PR's doc rewrite, and the agent confirmed only menu drop lines take styles.band while body cells wear bandItemFor placements. efe83f9 narrows the sentence to the menu-drop case.
guidance_note: When a doc sentence generalises a property over two cases (menu drop and disclosure body), check each case against the code path before writing it.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: efe83f9 only edited CLAUDE.md wording and added segment-colors tests, while `text: textOn(palette, tint)` is in the original decorationFor diff. The agent reproduced the bug before fixing it: on textual-dark, a body cell with bg: warning and no fg rendered #e0e0e0 where textOn(warning) is #121212. d7c6ecf makes text a function of the resolved bg.
guidance_note: When a derived value (contrast text) is computed from a base (tint) that an authored override (bg:) can replace, derive it from the resolved value at the point of resolution, and test the override-without-partner case.

narrative: Round 0 ran out of time after reviewing one of three scopes, so findings on the original diff came in over rounds 1-3. Every ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag here is a false positive: the named commits were narrow test or doc edits, and each finding targets code from the original PR. The one real defect (F5, text contrast chosen against the tint rather than an authored bg) was in the original decorationFor and was reproduced before the fix. No fix caused a later finding.
guidance_observations: The partial round-0 review spread original-PR findings over four rounds, so the round count overstates fix churn.
The agent reproduced F5 with concrete hex values before fixing it and pinned it with a unit test and an end-to-end test, which is the right pattern for a correctness finding.

evidence: `v === null` returns first, and `typeof undefined` is 'undefined', so `|| v === undefined` can never fire. 3068b25 deletes the clause.

The original runDoctorCli called gatherFacts with no try. settingsEnv throws on a malformed file, so the throw reached main's generic 'Error generating statusline' handler. 3068b25 catches it, writes `doctor:` plus the message to stderr, and exits 2.
guidance_note: When a CLI subcommand documents its own exit-code contract, route every throw from its fact-gathering into that contract, the way the sibling `check` command does.

evidence: The hint put a third DISCLOSURE_GLYPH_CLOSED after '🩺 doctor', but the reviewer and the agent's reply agree the doctor row is a plain action with no disclosure. 3068b25 changes the hint to '🩺 doctor, then [fix]'.
guidance_note: When a printed instruction names UI glyphs, build it from the actual menu structure rather than repeating a separator pattern.

evidence: The label is spliced into unquoted template body text (`✓ ${label}`), where escapeTemplateLiteral's \" escaping would render literally and protects nothing. The other call sites escape quoted arguments. 3068b25 drops the escape.
guidance_note: Before reusing an escaper, check that the splice context matches the one it was written for (quoted argument versus body text).

evidence: applyFix returns void, so its switch over fix.kind was not compiler-exhaustive. 3068b25 adds the `const _exhaustive: never = fix.kind` arm, the codebase's own idiom.
guidance_note: Every switch over a union discriminant in a void function gets the codebase's never-exhaustiveness arm when it is written.

evidence: doctorFix called gatherFacts (which probes tmux) before applyFix, then again inside writeReport. The fix re-reads only claudeSettingsEnv, which is the reviewer's own suggestion ('re-gathered only for state that applyFix could have changed') despite the different_fix label. That fix's hardcoded spread became F17.
guidance_note: When a handler needs pre- and post-effect facts, gather once and have the effect performer report what it changed, rather than re-gathering everything.

evidence: doctorRun decodes with oneArg, but the test helper listed VERB_DOCTOR_RUN in MULTI_ARG_VERBS. 3068b25 removes it. No test was added to pin the categorisation, which F28 later asked for.
guidance_note: When fixing a miscategorisation in a mirror table, add the test that would have caught it (the effectsOf per-verb decode case) in the same commit.

evidence: The JSON_DIALECT suite covered the empty-container and multi-line append branches but not the inline-member branch. 3068b25 adds `{ "env": { "A": "1" } }` and asserts JSON.parse round-trips.
guidance_note: When adding a dialect parameter to a splicer, run each existing branch of the splicer under the new dialect.

evidence: runDoctorCli exits 2 on any argument, but the help text listed only 0 and 1, while the sibling `check` entry lists all three. 3068b25 adds '2 usage error / unreadable settings'.
guidance_note: Write help text from the exit constants in the code (EXIT_USAGE), not from memory of the happy paths.

evidence: applyFix's read, splice and write are synchronous in one tick, so a compare-before-write would re-read the bytes it just read and close nothing. config-file-store's guard compares against a history snapshot from an earlier click, which applyFix does not have. The pushback stands on those facts; no-ambient-temporal-coupling does not describe this case.

Flag is a false positive: 3068b25 did not touch probeTmux's category or launch.ts RATE_LIMITS, and the uncapped click-driven synchronous spawn is original code. The first fix (719ff34) capped the shared `tmux` category, which broke the tmux segment's cache test in CI and needed 526a4e5. That cap then caused F21 and F22.
guidance_note: When adding a click-driven synchronous spawn, give it its own launch category with a rate limit; when capping an existing category, list every caller of that category first, then trace what each caller does with a rate-limited result.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 3068b25 did not touch main.rs, and detect_tmux is original code. The TS detectTmuxHint had a test table and the Rust mirror had none. 719ff34 factors out a pure tmux_hint and ports the table.
guidance_note: When mirroring a TS helper in Rust, follow the existing detect_term_extent pattern: a pure function over injected values plus the TS test table, in the same PR.

evidence: memberSet sorts away order, but the Rust TMUX_ENV array was read positionally, so a reorder would pass the check while swapping roles. The reviewer offered a named binding; the agent did that (a TmuxEnv struct) and also made the check compare role=VAR pairs.
guidance_note: When mirroring a named TS object in Rust, use a struct with the same field names rather than a positional array.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 3068b25 did not touch CLAUDE.md. The original PR added the tools paragraph and updated docs/interaction-authoring.md but left CLAUDE.md's row-1 enumeration without `🧰 tools`.
guidance_note: When adding an item to a UI row, grep the docs for every enumeration of that row and update each one.

evidence: The original PR added `|| actionBindsDoctor(a)` under a comment saying 'all five carry session.id', which is now stale. The agent rewrote the comment to state the rule instead of a count that drifts.
guidance_note: When adding an arm to a disjunction, update or de-count the comment that enumerates its arms in the same edit.

evidence: No test exercised doctorArm's validation (bad verb, unknown check, stray key) beside the set arm's existing cases. 719ff34 adds three cases, each isolating one failure, so the ordering bug in F27 stayed uncovered.
guidance_note: When adding a new validation arm, copy the sibling arms' negative tests, including one that combines failures to check every issue is reported in one pass.

evidence: The F6 fix in 3068b25 added `{ ...facts, claudeSettingsEnv: readClaudeSettingsEnv(...) }`, a per-fix-kind assumption that no exhaustive switch enforces. The same commit's F5 fix had just made applyFix exhaustive over Fix kind. The agent's fix (applyFix returns the post-fix facts) moves the knowledge into that one exhaustive switch.
guidance_note: When a fix adds behaviour that depends on a union variant (which fact a fix kind changes), put it inside the existing exhaustive switch over that union rather than hardcoding it beside the switch.

evidence: runDoctorCli had several exit paths and no test imported it. The try/catch path came from the F2 fix, but the untested CLI predates it. The agent split out a pure doctorPlan, mirroring check.ts, and tested exits 0, 1 and 2.
guidance_note: Write a new CLI subcommand as a pure plan plus a thin argv binding, like the existing `check`, so its exit paths are testable from the first commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the check-protocol row is original code. It diffed env-var names but not the inner wire-object keys socket/pane/truecolor, which both runtimes build independently. 719ff34 adds a `tmux hint wire keys` row.
guidance_note: When a new wire object crosses the TS/Rust mirror, add a check-protocol row for its field names alongside any vocabulary row.

evidence: 'CLAUDE_CODE_TMUX_TRUECOLOR' was spelled in both TMUX_ENV.truecolor and TMUX_TRUECOLOR_VAR in checks.ts, which already imported from tmux-hint. 719ff34 derives one from the other.
guidance_note: Before declaring a string constant, grep for the literal and derive from the existing declaration.

evidence: Before F11's fix there was no rate limit on the probe, so launchSync never returned 'rate-limited' there. The cap added in 719ff34/526a4e5 made that result reachable, and the probe's message composition doubled its prefix. The reviewer quoted the exact error string and the agent, who has the code, confirmed `error` is already a full sentence; launch.ts's error text is not in the packet.
guidance_note: When adding a rate limit to a spawn path, render the rate-limited result through each caller's error formatting once before pushing.

evidence: The category-wide cap from F11's fix means a [fix] click within 1 s of a doctor run gets a failed probe and the false 'nothing to fix'. The mislabel also applied to any failed probe before the cap, so the premise is real but overstated. The agent kept the cap and made the refusal carry the verdict's own reason.
guidance_note: When rate-limiting a path a user drives as a sequence (run, then fix), trace the second click inside the window and check what the user is told.

evidence: No earlier finding caused this: 3e0184e is an unprompted change that swapped ceil for round in minutesUntilReset and added `add 1` in the templates. The reviewer is right that it overstates (+90 min renders '1h 31m', pinned in cb3ed42), and right that it was uncommented and untested. The agent calls the +1 the maintainer's choice, but the packet shows no such decision, and the removed ceil already avoided '0m' without inflating.
guidance_note: An unrelated behaviour change riding a feature PR needs its WHY comment and a test of the shipped composition in the same commit; when replacing ceil with round+1, check that the new form beats the old one at the boundaries it changes.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 3e0184e did not touch edge.ts, and `JSON5.parse(text)` in settingsEnv is original code. That code contradicted its own module comment that Claude Code parses settings.json strictly. cb3ed42 adds Dialect.parse, reads through JSON_DIALECT, and pins a trailing-comma file to exit 2.
guidance_note: When a module states that a consumer is strict about a format, use that same strictness for both reading and writing; the writer already used JSON_DIALECT while the reader used JSON5.

evidence: This duplicates F23 in the same round, on unprompted commit 3e0184e, and no earlier finding caused it. It adds that the duration test still pinned the un-wrapped composition, which is true per the 3e0184e diff. It was resolved in cb3ed42 alongside F23, with the same unverified 'deliberate' claim.

Flag is a false positive: cb3ed42 did not touch the schema or config-schema tests. The doctor arm was the only action arm without GOOD/BAD_STRUCTURAL cases in config-schema.test.ts. 3823896 adds them.
guidance_note: When adding an action arm, add it to every per-arm test table, including the schema artifact's GOOD/BAD lists, not only the loader tests.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: cb3ed42 did not touch actions.ts. The original doctorArm returns null on a bad verb before its unknown-key loop, unlike the sibling arms, so it does not report all issues in one pass. The fix is right, but the problem is consistency with the arms' report-every-issue convention, not dataflow versus control flow.
guidance_note: When writing a new arm beside existing ones, copy their check order (unknown keys first, unconditionally) rather than reinventing it.

evidence: F7's fix in 3068b25 only removed VERB_DOCTOR_RUN from MULTI_ARG_VERBS. No effectsOf test pins either doctor verb's decode, so the same miscategorisation could come back silently. 3823896 adds the two cases.
guidance_note: A fix for a miscategorisation is not complete until a test fails on the old categorisation.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: sessionHints is original code that cb3ed42 did not touch. The reachable 'has not rendered yet' branch had no test. The agent added that test and kept the not-JSON and not-object arms as the string seam's parser, matching the reviewer's own scoping.
guidance_note: Test each loud-refusal branch of a new verb that a real click can reach, such as a session that has never rendered.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the plain writeFileSync to settings.json is in the original applyFix, and cb3ed42 did not touch it. A crash mid-write can truncate the file, while config-file-store already had writeAtomic. 3823896 extracts writeAtomic into a shared util used by both settings.json writers.
guidance_note: When writing a file another program depends on, reach for the repo's existing tmp-and-rename writer instead of writeFileSync.

narrative: Most findings target original-PR code, and most ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags are false positives because the named commits never touched the flagged files. The real fix-caused chains: F11's rate limit (first put on the shared `tmux` category, which broke a CI test) produced both round-2 findings, a doubled error prefix and a misleading 'nothing to fix'. F6's single-probe fix hardcoded which fact a fix changes (F17), and F7's fix shipped without a pinning test (F28). Round 3 came from an unprompted countdown change (3e0184e) that inflated displayed minutes, plus an original JSON5-versus-strict-JSON read gap. The one pushback (F10, TOCTOU) was correct on the facts.
guidance_observations: Round 2 existed only because of the F11 fix: the cap was added without listing the category's other callers or tracing what a rate-limited result does downstream.

An unrelated behaviour change (the countdown +1) rode the doctor PR without a comment or test and cost a round. The agent defended it as the maintainer's choice, but nothing in the thread records that decision.

Several round-1 and round-4 findings were missing tests that the sibling arms already had (doctorArm negatives, schema GOOD/BAD, effectsOf decode); copying the sibling test tables when adding an arm would have removed them up front.
